Solution:
Suppose that (V, T1) and (V, T2) are two trees defined over a common vertex set
V . Prove that for every edge e in the edge set T1, there exists a corresponding edge f in T2
such that exchanging these edges preserves the tree structure for both graphs; that is, prove
that (V, (T1 \ {e}) ∪{f}) and (V, (T2 \ {f}) ∪{e}) are both trees.
Theorem 1. Let (V, T1) and (V, T2) be two trees on a common vertex set V . For every edge
e ∈T1, there exists an edge f ∈T2 such that both (V, (T1\{e})∪{f}) and (V, (T2\{f})∪{e})
are trees.
Proof. Let e = (u, v) ∈T1 be an arbitrary edge.
Since T1 is a tree, removing edge e
disconnects T1 into exactly two connected components. Denote these components as C1
(containing vertex u) and C2 (containing vertex v).
Define the set of crossing edges in T2:
F = {(x, y) ∈T2 : x ∈C1 and y ∈C2}
Lemma 1. F ̸= ∅
Proof of Lemma. Since T2 is a tree on vertex set V , it is connected. Therefore, there exists
a path in T2 from any vertex in C1 to any vertex in C2. In particular, there is a path from
u ∈C1 to v ∈C2. Any such path must contain at least one edge with one endpoint in C1
and the other in C2, hence F ̸= ∅.
Now consider the unique path P from u to v in T2. Since u ∈C1 and v ∈C2, this path
must use at least one edge from F. Let f = (x, y) ∈F be any edge on this path P, with
x ∈C1 and y ∈C2.
We claim that f satisfies the required properties.
Part 1: (T1 \ {e}) ∪{f} is a tree.
After removing edge e, the graph T1 \ {e} has:
• |V | vertices
• |V | −2 edges (since |T1| = |V | −1)
• Two connected components: C1 and C2
Adding edge f = (x, y) with x ∈C1 and y ∈C2:
• Increases the edge count to |V | −1
• Connects the two components C1 and C2 into a single connected component
• Creates no cycle, since f joins two previously disconnected components
Therefore, (T1 \ {e}) ∪{f} is a connected graph on |V | vertices with |V | −1 edges, hence
it is a tree.
Part 2: (T2 \ {f}) ∪{e} is a tree.
Removing edge f from T2 creates two components:
• D1: the component containing vertex x
• D2: the component containing vertex y
Since f lies on the path P from u to v in T2:
• The subpath of P from u to x does not use edge f, so this path exists in T2 \ {f}.
Therefore u ∈D1.
• The subpath of P from y to v does not use edge f, so this path exists in T2 \ {f}.
Therefore v ∈D2.
Thus, u and v are in different components of T2 \ {f}. Adding edge e = (u, v):
• Increases the edge count from |V | −2 to |V | −1
• Connects components D1 and D2 into a single connected component
• Creates no cycle, since e joins two previously disconnected components
Therefore, (T2 \ {f}) ∪{e} is a connected graph on |V | vertices with |V | −1 edges, hence
it is a tree.
This completes the proof.
